candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall ensure that the sewage sludge meets the requirements in 40 CFR 258 concerning the quality of the sludge dispose d in a municipal solid waste landfill unit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpreting which 40 CFR 258 pollutant criteria apply, and whether sludge quality measurements are compared against those incorporated limits, changes which enforceable numeric limits govern MSWLF sludge disposal and whether reported values exceed them.

candidates.exact_span: If requirements for sludge management practices or pollutant criteria become more stringent than the sludge pollutant limits or acceptable management practices in this permit, or control a pollutant not listed in this permit, this permit may be modified or revoked and reissued to conform to the requirements promulgated at Section 405(d)(2) of the Clean Water Act.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether and when more stringent Section 405(d)(2) criteria supersede the permit's stated sludge pollutant limits or management practices changes which numeric limits and management-based obligations are in force during Federal FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested once during the life of the permit within one year from the effective date of the permit in accordance with the method specified at 40 CFR 268, Appendix I (Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP)) or other approved methods.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 'once during the life of the permit within one year' window and allowance for 'other approved methods' affect whether TCLP monitoring was required during FY2025 and whether absence of a TCLP result reflects a satisfied one-time obligation, an unmet requirement, or unresolved applicability.

candidates.exact_span: Sludge shall be tested after final treatment prior to leaving the POTW site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The timing condition 'after final treatment prior to leaving the POTW site' determines which disposal events trigger the TCLP obligation and whether monitoring evidence from other points or times satisfies the requirement.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 261, shall be handled according to RCRA standards for the disposal of hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 262.
candidates.computation_change_reason: How 'determined to be a hazardous waste' under 40 CFR Part 261 is interpreted switches the applicable compliance framework from MSWLF sludge limits to RCRA hazardous-waste standards and associated monitoring/handling obligations.

candidates.exact_span: The disposal of sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste, in other than a certified hazardous waste disposal facility shall be prohibited.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This prohibition is an enforceable limit on disposal pathway; different interpretations of hazardous-waste status or what counts as a 'certified hazardous waste disposal facility' change whether a disposal action exceeds applicable limits.

candidates.exact_span: The report will contain test results, certification that unauthorized disposal has not occurred and a summary of alternative disposal plans that comply with RCRA standards for the disposal of hazardous waste.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The required 'certification that unauthorized disposal has not occurred' after a TCLP failure defines what documentary evidence must exist to classify periods with no ordinary numeric result as documented no-discharge/unauthorized-disposal states versus unresolved missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested as needed, or at a minimum, once/year in accordance with the method 9095 (Paint Filter Liquids Test) as described in "Test Methods for Evaluating Solid Wastes, Physical/Chemical Methods" (EPA Pub. No. SW-846).
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 'as needed, or at a minimum, once/year' frequency and method 9095 criterion determine whether Paint Filter monitoring was required in each FY2025 period and whether a missing result reflects conditional non-requirement, satisfied annual monitoring, or inadequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Recordkeeping requirements - The permittee shall develop the following information and shall retain the information for five years.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The obligation to develop and retain specified information for five years affects whether monitoring and disposal evidence is expected to exist for FY2025 evaluations and how absent records are classified when the segment does not enumerate the required fields in this excerpt.
